summary: Intermittent 500s + elevated latency during us-east -> us-west failover (Dedicated)
body:
Customer reported intermittent HTTP 500s and elevated p95 latency during an automatic regional failover event impacting their Dedicated deployment. Symptoms began shortly after Redwood initiated a traffic shift from us-east to us-west due to upstream instability in us-east. Errors were intermittent (bursty), correlating with routing policy changes and capacity warm-up in the target region.

---
Issue Summary
- Customer: Acme AI (Dedicated)
- Start time (customer observed): 2025-10-21 17:41Z
- End time (mitigated): 2025-10-21 19:06Z
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (primary), /v1/embeddings (minor)
- Impact: ~1.8% request error rate peak (500s), p95 latency elevated from ~480ms to 1.6–2.4s for chat; customer experienced retries and partial request failures.

Customer Impact (from Acme)
- 500s caused request failures in their app tier even with retries (some requests not retried due to idempotency constraints).
- Latency spikes triggered their internal circuit breaker, reducing traffic and causing downstream degradation.
- Customer asked whether this should be expected behavior during failover and what remediation/SLA expectations are.

Environment
- Dedicated deployment: acme-ai-dedicated-prod
- Primary region: us-east
- Failover/secondary region: us-west
- Models pinned: redwood-llama-70b-instruct (chat), redwood-embed-large-v3 (embeddings)

---
Timeline (UTC)
- 2025-10-21 17:36Z: Fleet alerts on us-east capacity health degradation (GPU node health checks failing). Automated failover policy begins shifting routing weights.
- 2025-10-21 17:41Z: Customer opens ticket reporting intermittent 500s + latency.
- 2025-10-21 17:48Z: Support acknowledges, requests request_ids + timestamps; links customer to status page note (internal-only draft).
- 2025-10-21 17:52Z: SRE engages in #incidents; incident commander requests classification for incident taxonomy pilot.
- 2025-10-21 18:03Z: Routing team observes elevated fallback attempts and increased gateway upstream timeout errors during weight changes.
- 2025-10-21 18:12Z: Fleet begins accelerating warm capacity in us-west for acme pool; provisioning lag ~12–18 minutes.
- 2025-10-21 18:24Z: Temporary mitigation: slow down weight ramp (reduce step size), increase request hedging thresholds, and disable one policy rule that was aggressively failing over per-POP.
- 2025-10-21 18:38Z: Error rate decreases; latency still elevated for longer prompts.
- 2025-10-21 18:51Z: Additional GPUs online; routing stabilizes; p95 improves.
- 2025-10-21 19:06Z: Incident declared mitigated; monitoring shows steady-state error rate <0.1% and p95 back near baseline.
- 2025-10-22: Follow-up to customer with incident summary and next steps.

Internal links
- Slack incident thread: https://slack.com/archives/CINCIDENTS/p1762210207 ("INC-2025-10-21-USE1-Failover")
- Relevant support coordination: #support (internal), thread cross-linked in incident channel
- Dashboards (internal):
  - Dedicated gateway errors by customer: grafana://dedicated/gateway-errors?customer=acme-ai
  - Router fallback reasons: grafana://routing/fallback-reasons?customer=acme-ai
  - Fleet capacity warm-up: grafana://fleet/capacity?pool=acme-ai-usw

---
Customer-provided examples
1) Chat completion 500
- Timestamp: 2025-10-21T17:44:19Z
- Request ID: req_01JAX7Q2F6K8H0T2E0P8R5X9Q1
- Response: 500
- Customer note: occurred during retry burst; second attempt succeeded.

2) Chat completion high latency
- Timestamp: 2025-10-21T18:05:11Z
- Request ID: req_01JAX82G8Z2M2R9V5VQH8A3P2T
- Observed latency: 2.38s (normally <600ms)

---
Redwood investigation notes
Observed symptoms
- API gateway saw spikes in upstream timeout and "no healthy backends" for a subset of traffic during the routing weight shift.
- Smart routing emitted a sharp increase in fallback attempts with mixed reasons:
  - capacity (target pool warm-up)
  - health (backend health flapping during ramp)
  - timeout (gateway waiting on backends during rebalancing)

Representative internal logs (sanitized)
- gateway (us-west):
  - 2025-10-21T17:44:19.122Z level=error msg="upstream request failed" request_id=req_01JAX7Q2F6K8H0T2E0P8R5X9Q1 upstream_status=504 route=chat_completions customer=acme-ai region=us-west
  - 2025-10-21T17:44:19.124Z level=error msg="mapped upstream failure to 500" request_id=req_01JAX7Q2F6K8H0T2E0P8R5X9Q1
- router:
  - 2025-10-21T17:44:18.981Z level=warn msg="fallback applied" request_id=req_01JAX7Q2F6K8H0T2E0P8R5X9Q1 from_region=us-east to_region=us-west fallback_reason=capacity
  - 2025-10-21T18:03:02.447Z level=warn msg="fallback applied" request_id=req_01JAX82G8Z2M2R9V5VQH8A3P2T from_region=us-east to_region=us-west fallback_reason=health

Hypothesis and conclusion
- Primary contributing factor: insufficient warm capacity in us-west for Acme’s dedicated pool during a rapid failover ramp, causing backend health to flap under sudden load.
- Secondary contributing factor: routing policy ramp steps were too aggressive for this pool’s scale, amplifying transient "no healthy backends" windows.
- Not observed: model/runtime regression (no correlated OOM/scheduler stall spikes), auth/RBAC, or customer misconfiguration.

Proposed incident taxonomy mapping (for taxonomy pilot validation)
- Candidate primary incident_type: Capacity/Fleet Shortage > Regional warm capacity / provisioning lag
- Candidate alternate (considered): Routing/Fallback Misbehavior > Policy ramp / health gating overly aggressive
- Decision (internal): classify as Capacity/Fleet (primary) with Routing as contributing system.
  - Rationale: the failure mode only presented because target region did not have sufficient warmed capacity; routing behavior was within configured policy bounds but the ramp configuration lacked guardrails.

Owner mapping (informal, pending v1 taxonomy signoff)
- Primary: Infra/Fleet
- Secondary/Consulted: Platform Smart Routing

---
Mitigation / Resolution
Immediate mitigations applied during incident
- Reduced routing weight ramp step size for failover policy for acme-ai pool.
- Increased pre-warm capacity target in us-west and accelerated provisioning.
- Temporarily adjusted health gating thresholds to reduce flapping during ramp.

Customer-facing resolution
- 500s and elevated latency resolved once us-west pool reached steady capacity and routing weights stabilized.
- Support confirmed with customer that error rate and latency returned to baseline by 19:10Z.

---
Follow-ups / action items
1) Fleet: add dedicated-pool-specific warm capacity guardrail for automated failovers (target: ensure N minutes of headroom before ramp >X%).
2) Routing: add safer default ramp profile and "abort/slowdown" logic when backend health flaps during weight changes.
3) Support/CS: update Dedicated incident comms guidance for failover scenarios (what to expect, how to interpret transient errors).
4) Taxonomy program: include this ticket as an example case in the taxonomy workshop (capacity vs routing boundary).

---
Comments (excerpt)
- 2025-10-21 17:48Z (Dev Patel, Support): "Thanks — we’re seeing a concurrent us-east instability event and are shifting your Dedicated traffic to us-west. Can you share 2–3 request IDs around 17:40–18:00Z? We’ll correlate in logs and keep you updated every 30 minutes until stable."
- 2025-10-21 18:09Z (Acme AI, Customer): "Confirming the 500s are intermittent. Retrying helps but latency is still elevated. Is this expected during failover?"
- 2025-10-21 18:27Z (Rafael Mendes, SRE): "We’re mitigating by slowing the ramp and warming capacity. Current hypothesis is target-region warm capacity lag. Next update in ~20 minutes."
- 2025-10-21 19:12Z (Dev Patel, Support): "Metrics indicate stability is restored (errors <0.1%, latency near baseline). We’ll share a post-incident summary + prevention steps tomorrow."

Resolution code
- Resolution: Mitigated (configuration + capacity warm-up)
- Customer confirmation: Yes (2025-10-22 16:05Z via email)
